title: Semiconductor Fab Tool Predictive Maintenance
thesis: Snowflake turns readings from 24 synthetic fab tools at five fictional Malaysian sites into availability KPIs, 7-day down-risk scores, vibration anomalies and grounded AI answers, all on curated dynamic tables.

talking_points: Tool availability, unscheduled downs, mean time between downs and tools tracked across Penang, Kulim, Melaka, Ipoh and Kuching.
Every KPI is a numerator over a denominator in a curated dynamic table, so it traces back to tool-day rows.
The root-cause chart shows RF generator faults and CVD heater drift costing the most hours.
tabs.call_out: One governed set of fab maintenance KPIs, traceable to source rows

transition.line: Which tools are likely to go down next?

talking_points: Snowflake ML classification scores each tool's probability of an unscheduled down in the next 7 days.
The holdout line shows precision and recall on the most recent days, against the base rate.
Anomaly detection flags pump vibration outliers per tool, and the forecast projects fab-wide downtime for 14 days.
tabs.call_out: Honest, evaluated ML inside the data platform

transition.line: Do we have the spares to respond?

talking_points: Critical spares on order and spare coverage (RF match units, heater assemblies, capillary sets, probe cards) frame response capacity.
PM compliance against yield by tool shows where discipline and output move together; it is an association, not proof of cause.
The action memo drafts three prioritised tool actions from the KPI, downtime and risk tables only.
tabs.call_out: Grounded draft actions, with a human in the loop

transition.line: What happens when a chamber alarms right now?

talking_points: Live readings land in RAW.LIVE_TELEMETRY, from the simulator or from AWS IoT Core through Snowpipe.
The Snowflake alert logs ALARM readings with an SOP hint and the tool's current risk band, then emails the on-call equipment engineer.
tabs.call_out: From tool alarm to action in one platform

talking_points: The Cortex Agent uses Cortex Analyst over the semantic view for metrics, and Cortex Search over 15 synthetic fab tool SOPs.
Each answer shows the generated SQL and the SOPs it cited.

transition.line: Here is how it is built.

talking_points: Two builds share one core: Snowflake only, or AWS + Snowflake (IoT Core, Bedrock, QuickSight and Amazon Q).
Everything shown is synthetic demo data, rebuilt reproducibly from the repo.
tabs.call_out: One governed core, with an optional AWS edge
